subject: Pilot throughput snapshot — clarifying token/QPS thresholds and fallback SLOs
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Zhang <emma@openpilot.ai>, ops@openpilot.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot throughput snapshot — clarifying token/QPS thresholds and fallback SLOs

Hey Emma / OpenPilot team — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and requested confirmations so we can size the pilot and lock the SLOs: 

- Observed peak vs baseline: we heard "short" peaks and sustained baseline. Please confirm the highest sustained 5‑minute average QPS and the single-minute peak during your busiest hour. We recorded ~120 QPS baseline on our notes, but I want the numbers from your telemetry.
- Payloads / token counts: you mentioned ~1k–1.5k tokens for the typical annotation request and up to ~4k tokens for long transcripts. Can you attach a small sample (10–20 rows) with token counts and whether responses are streaming?
- Streaming concurrency: you called out concurrent streaming sessions — please confirm max concurrent live streams you see. We need that to set KV cache sizing and streaming SLO targets.
- Latency target: you said the product team expects ~p95 < 500ms for non‑streamed calls with p90 ~300ms for short requests. Confirm which percentile the contract should target (p95 vs p90) and whether warm KV cache is required for the SLO to apply.
- Fallback policy: per our discussion we'll propose an automated fallback to a smaller quantized variant when latency or capacity thresholds are hit. Confirm whether degraded quality during fallback is acceptable for up to 10% of requests during 5‑minute surge windows.

Next steps (action owners):
- OpenPilot: share a 10–20 row sample CSV with request token sizes, per‑request QPS timestamps if possible (Emma) — by EOD Monday.
- Redwood (me): produce an initial capacity estimate + cost delta for a 30‑day pilot (includes burst capacity windows) and a draft SLA that implements the percentile and fallback policy — by Tuesday 6/22.
- Redwood (Marissa / Priyom): quick ops sync to validate streaming concurrency assumptions and autoscale floor.

Attachments: placeholder profile we'll use to collect samples: openpilot_token_profile.csv (please populate).

Thanks —
Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
From: Emma Zhang <emma@openpilot.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: OpenPilot Ops <ops@openpilot.ai>, procurement@openpilot.ai
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot throughput snapshot — clarifying token/QPS thresholds and fallback SLOs

Karthik — thanks for the detailed recap. Confirming and adding context below: 

- Peak vs baseline: our production telemetry shows a baseline of ~110–130 QPS during workday hours and short spikes up to 420 QPS (single‑minute peak) on heavy ingestion events (usually under 2 minutes). The 5‑minute rolling peak averages max at ~260 QPS.
- Token counts: attached sample (openpilot_token_profile.csv) with 15 rows. Typical requests are ~1,200 tokens; long transcripts can be 3,500–4,000 tokens but those are <5% of volume.
- Streaming concurrency: concurrent live sessions hit 32–38 in our largest markets (US‑west), typically for 60–90s windows. They are rare elsewhere.
- Latency percentile target: product prefers p95 < 500ms for interactive endpoints. Engineering would prefer the SLO to be p90=300ms as an internal target; for contract/SLA we should use p95=500ms with a specified warm‑cache caveat.
- Fallback: acceptable to have up to 10% of requests routed to a smaller variant during a sustained capacity issue. We do need an explicit statement on how quality regressions will be measured for acceptance testing.

Other notes: we require US region routing for this pilot. Procurement will review the SLA; please cc procurement@openpilot.ai on the draft.

Attached: openpilot_token_profile.csv (sample filled)

—Emma
Emma Zhang
Head of Platform, OpenPilot
emma@openpilot.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Pilot throughput snapshot — clarifying token/QPS thresholds and fallback SLOs

Karthik / Priyom — quick internal readout and recommended sizing approach based on the OpenPilot numbers Emma pasted: 

- Use a medium‑quantized 8‑bit variant for baseline traffic to keep unit costs down; keep N=2 replica floor (2 GPUs) with autoscale to N=6 for burst. That maps to handling ~120 QPS sustained and up to ~420 QPS for short windows with acceptable p95 latency headroom if we enable aggressive batching and prefix cache.
- Streaming: reserve 1 GPU of streaming-optimized instances dedicated (or a streaming slot equivalent) with a concurrency limit of ~40 to cover peaks; implement per‑client throttles if sessions exceed 60s to avoid tail saturation.
- SLA draft: set contract SLO = p95 < 500ms for non‑streamed endpoints in US, with 5‑minute interruption windows allowed for fallback. Track quality regressions by a 200‑sample eval set (OpenPilot to provide).

I'll sync with infra Ops tomorrow to validate that autoscale timing and GPU provisioning match these numbers. If anyone sees a misassumption, flag now.

—Marissa
Director, Performance & SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Zhang <emma@openpilot.ai>, OpenPilot Ops <ops@openpilot.ai>, procurement@openpilot.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 09:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot throughput snapshot — clarifying token/QPS thresholds and fallback SLOs

Emma — appreciate the sample and confirmations. Next actions from our side: 

1) Capacity & cost estimate: we'll circulate a short spreadsheet outlining a 30‑day pilot configuration (baseline N=2, burst up to N=6 for 60s windows, separate streaming slot) with projected token cost and estimated monthly run rate by EOD Tuesday (attached: SLA‑draft‑OpenPilot.pdf and the populated token profile).
2) SLA draft: included is a p95=500ms contract target with a warm‑cache clause and a fallback plan. Please review and point out any hard procurement items.
3) Acceptance/test criteria: Emma — please send the 200‑sample eval set or grant us access to a reproducible scoring job. We will use it to measure quality regression for fallback events.
4) Ops runbook: Priyom / Marissa — can you schedule a 30‑minute call with OpenPilot Ops to walk through autoscale settings and emergency fallbacks? Prefer Mon 6/28 or Tue 6/29 morning PST.

Thanks — will follow up with the capacity spreadsheet and cost delta in a separate note.

Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
